To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
conscientiousness is positively and agreeableness is negatively related to entrepreneurial failure.
agreeable entrepreneurs are more likely to succeed, and conscientious entrepreneurs are more likely fail, but only at the time launching their firm.

conscientious entrepreneurs have a higher probability to fail at the start up of the business, but that they have a lower failure probability over time, whereas agreeableness reduces the failure probability at all times from start up.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the personality traits of highly innovative entrepreneurs.
the relationship between personality and entrepreneurial failure in the context of highly innovative industries.
the relationship between personality and entrepreneurial failure in a highly innovative industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the personality profile of agreeableness is a key factor for entrepreneurial failure, but only in highly innovative industries and in combination with conscientiousness.
the Big-Five theory of personality is not sufficient to predict entrepreneurial failure in highly dynamic environments.
agreeableness is the key personality trait to be successful in highly innovative industries, whereas conscientiousness increases failure hazard rates at the beginning of a firm’s life cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
conscientiousness is a personality trait of highly innovative effectuators, while agreeableness is a personality trait for highly innovative entrepreneurs.
conscientious entrepreneurs are more likely to fail in the beginning, whereas agreeable entrepreneurs are less prone to fail in the end.
agreeableness and conscientiousness are the two personality traits that are most likely to influence the probability of entrepreneurial failure in the long run.
The main takeaway from our work is that
conscientiousness and agreeableness are the most important personality traits for entrepreneurial success in highly innovative industries.

the relationship between the comprehensive personality traits of highly innovative entrepreneurs is not linear but nonlinear and thus the failure hazard rate of entrepreneurs in the highly innovative industries is not only a function of personality traits but also of time.
the Big-Five model is a suitable framework to explain entrepreneurial failure in highly dynamic environments.
